title: NDT Report Validation in Houston, TX | Independent Review
description: Independent review of NDT reports and digital inspection data from Houston refineries, chemical plants, LNG and pipelines, checked against the code.
h1: Independent NDT report review for the Houston Ship Channel, Baytown, Texas City and Freeport
intro: Houston produces inspection paperwork on an industrial scale. Refinery turnarounds on the ship channel, chemical plant outages in Baytown and Freeport, LNG maintenance on Quintana Island, pipeline digs and a steady stream of shop-fabricated vessels all end in reports somebody has to accept, pay for or defend. We review those reports, and the digital inspection data behind them, independently against the procedure, the code edition and the owner's specification, then set out in writing what the evidence supports. Atlantis's US office is in Houston, but the review itself is still carried out remotely on the records you send.

highlights.p: A Gulf Coast turnaround can close with hundreds of reports from a dozen contractors in a few weeks. The review can cover a risk-ranked sample, one disputed package or a full close-out set, and the scope is agreed before a single file moves.

Operators, inspection contractors, shops, insurers and deal teams ask for reviews for different reasons. We start by asking which decision rides on the record, and the reviewer concentrates on the checks that decide it.

Encoded PAUT and TOFD files, CR and DR images, eddy current tube files and corrosion maps from Houston-area jobs are opened in review software and compared with the dispositions written in the report.

sections.h: Who asks for independent report reviews around Houston
p: The Houston area packs refining, chemicals, gas processing, LNG export and pipeline terminals into a handful of counties, and nearly every asset in it is inspected on a cycle. ExxonMobil runs its integrated refining and chemical complex at Baytown. The Deer Park refinery on the ship channel belongs to PEMEX. Chevron owns the Pasadena refinery, where it completed upgrades in late 2024. Valero operates refineries in Houston and Texas City, and Marathon Petroleum's Galveston Bay refinery in Texas City is, in the EIA's 2026 capacity data, the largest in the country on a stream-day basis, at 678,000 barrels per stream day. Further south, Dow's Texas Operations in Freeport is the company's largest integrated manufacturing site, with Freeport LNG's export terminal close by on Quintana Island, and to the east Enterprise Products operates NGL fractionation at Mont Belvieu.

In a region like this, independent reviews are normally commissioned by someone one step removed from the examination: an owner's reliability or inspection group accepting a contractor's work, a contractor answering a rejection from the owner's inspector, a fabricator whose data book has been held at receipt, an insurer adjusting a claim after an outage, or a deal team reading inspection files before an acquisition closes. Construction and warranty lawyers make up much of the rest. All of them need the same thing, a reader with no stake in the result who can say whether the record would survive scrutiny.

Ownership change is part of the local picture too. LyondellBasell ended refining at its Houston refinery in March 2025. On 30 October 2026 Valero said it had agreed to buy the idled plant and aimed to restart 165,000 barrels per day of crude processing by the end of 2027; the purchase had not closed when this page was written. Restarting any idled unit leans heavily on the inspection history written before it stopped, and on whether records for equipment left standing can still be trusted. Reviews of legacy inspection files are a normal part of that kind of work.

sections.h: Codes and regulators behind a Houston inspection record
p: Most process equipment in Houston plants sits inside OSHA's process safety management standard, 29 CFR 1910.119. Its mechanical integrity element expects every inspection and test on covered equipment to be written down with when it was done, who did it, which equipment it concerned, what the test was and what it found. Owners meet that expectation through API 510, 570 and 653 programs and their own engineering standards, so the report is read against the owner's program as well as against the code.

Boilers follow a separate track. The Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation issues boiler certificates of operation for periods of one to three years, and certificate inspections are made either by TDLR's deputy inspectors or by authorized inspectors employed by authorized inspection agencies. A report on boiler tubes or drums therefore has two readers: the owner's reliability engineer and the inspector whose visit keeps the certificate current.

Pipelines split by jurisdiction. Interstate lines answer to PHMSA, whose Southwest Region office is in Houston, while intrastate transmission, distribution and regulated gathering lines fall to the Railroad Commission of Texas, which adopts the federal minimum standards by reference. LNG facilities add 49 CFR Part 193, which incorporates NFPA 59A. Texas is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography licences and radiographer certification are handled by the Department of State Health Services under 25 TAC §289.255, with NRC Region IV in Arlington carrying the agency's remaining duties in the state. Atlantis does not perform industrial radiography in Texas; radiographs and digital images from your licensed contractor are reviewed as documents.

sections.h: Turnaround close-out on the ship channel
p: A large Gulf Coast turnaround ends with reports from several inspection contractors, each using its own templates and its own digital reporting system, and the owner's inspectors have days rather than weeks to decide which items can go back into service. Independent review earns its place here when it is targeted. We normally agree a risk-ranked sample with the owner: items carrying rejectable or borderline findings, repairs, equipment whose inspection technique changed since the last outage, and packages from contractors new to the site.

Many close-out findings are clerical rather than technical: thickness readings filed against CML numbers that no longer match the owner's database, PAUT scans saved without their setup file, repair welds whose final examination report cites the original weld's procedure, and calibration certificates for an instrument that left site before the work it supposedly covers. The opinion classes each one as a documentation gap or as something that undermines the accept or reject decision, so the owner knows which items can be released once the paperwork is corrected and which need an engineering call.

sections.h: Vendor data books from Houston fabrication shops
p: The metro area has a deep bench of shops building ASME Section VIII vessels, shell-and-tube exchangers, B31.3 piping spools and process skids for plants in Texas and overseas. Their data books often decide whether equipment is accepted at delivery, and one missing radiograph or an unsigned UT report can hold a shipment on the dock.

A fabricator review checks that the examination extent matches the joint category and what the code requires, that film or DR images reach the image quality the procedure demands, that ultrasonic examination used instead of radiography was allowed by the code and by the purchase order, and that PMI and hardness results belong to the welds listed. Overseas buyers often ask for this before equipment leaves Houston, because a data book is far easier to correct at the shop than after it has crossed an ocean.
list: Weld maps that agree with the drawings and with the NDT reports, joint by joint
Welder and NDT personnel certificates valid on the dates the work was done
Image quality indicators and density or signal-to-noise values on every radiograph or DR image
UT technique sheets and scan coverage wherever UT replaced radiography
PMI, hardness and material traceability records tied to individual welds
Hydrotest charts with calibrated gauges and the witnessing signatures the specification asks for

sections.h: Pipelines, terminals and equipment returning to service
p: Houston is a pipeline hub, and girth weld records reach review for new laterals, terminal tie-ins and replacement sections. Under 49 CFR Part 195, girth welds at hazardous liquid tie-ins must be nondestructively tested over their full circumference, the testing has to follow written procedures, and each weld has to be interpreted against the acceptance standard. The reviewer checks that the radiographs, DR images or automated UT data cover every tie-in on the alignment sheet and that each interpretation cites the right criteria.

Storage terminals around the ship channel produce API 653 shell and floor reports, MFL floor scans and settlement surveys. Equipment coming back from a long idle period raises a different question: whether the last inspection before shutdown still describes its condition, and whether preservation records exist at all. The opinion says what the existing record can support and where only new examination will answer the question.

sections.h: Digital inspection data and digital reporting from Houston work
p: Inspection work in Houston plants is now digital from acquisition to sign-off. Contractors load thickness readings into the owner's inspection data management system, PAUT and TOFD files sit on project drives, CR and DR images move between companies in DICONDE or vendor formats, and reports are issued from digital reporting platforms with electronic signatures. That gives an independent reviewer more to work with, because the data can be reopened, but it also creates new places for a record to go wrong.

We follow data lineage from the raw file to the issued report: which instrument file produced which reading, whether a DR image was reprocessed after it was interpreted, whether the electronic signature belongs to someone certified on the date shown, and whether an imported reading landed against the right CML. When an owner moves to a new digital reporting platform, a review of a sample of migrated records shows whether the inspection history survived the move intact.

sections.h: How a review runs when your records are in Houston
p: Atlantis's US office is in Houston, and many scoping conversations start there, but the review is carried out remotely on the records you send through secure transfer. There is no laboratory, inspection crew or field team behind it, and nobody needs a gate pass to your site. The office in Hyderabad shares the work when volume calls for it.

sections.h: Who reviews the records, and where the review stops
p: Ultrasonic, radiographic, magnetic particle, penetrant and visual records are reviewed under an ASNT NDT Level III who holds certification in all five of those methods. For eddy current tube data, MFL floor scans or acoustic emission, the proposal names a reviewer with the certification your contract calls for. Behind that Level III sits a review team whose members come from nuclear, maritime, oil and gas and petrochemical work.

The opinion covers the inspection record. Remaining-life, fitness-for-service and rerating calculations stay with your engineer, and the inspector of record for a vessel or piping system stays the person your program names. Atlantis does not review reports on work it performed and does not certify personnel. Where the review shows new examination is needed, the opinion describes the technique that would close the gap, and choosing the contractor to do it remains the owner's decision.

faqs.q: Atlantis has an office in Houston. Will a reviewer come to our plant?
faqs.a: No. The Houston office handles conversations and scoping, but the review is a remote document and data review carried out on the files you send. Nothing in it needs site access, and no inspection crew is involved.

faqs.q: Can you review a contractor's turnaround package before the unit restarts?
faqs.a: Yes, and a targeted sample usually serves better than a full read. We agree with you which items carry the most risk, such as repairs, borderline findings and work by contractors new to the site, and the opinion separates paperwork gaps from findings that affect the disposition.

faqs.q: Do you review radiographs shot by our licensed radiography contractor?
faqs.a: Yes. Film radiographs, CR and DR images are checked for image quality, coverage and interpretation as part of the weld record. Atlantis does not carry out radiography in Texas, where industrial radiography is licensed by the Department of State Health Services.

faqs.q: A buyer has held our data book at receipt. Can an independent review help?
faqs.a: It can. We read the data book against the code and the purchase order, and the opinion tells you which items are genuine nonconformances and which are documentation that can be supplied or corrected. Many shops send it to the buyer as the basis for closing the hold.

faqs.q: Which codes do you review Houston-area reports against?
faqs.a: Whatever governed the work: ASME Section V with Section VIII or B31.3, API 510, 570 and 653, API 1104, AWS D1.1, the owner's engineering standards, and 49 CFR Parts 192, 193 and 195 for gas, LNG and liquid pipelines. The opinion states which edition and table each decision rests on.

faqs.q: Can the review support a decision on idled equipment returning to service?
faqs.a: It tells you which existing records are still reliable and where the history has gaps. Decisions on condition, rerating or fitness-for-service stay with your engineer, who can use the opinion to decide what new examination is needed before start-up.

faqs.q: Do you review eddy current tube data from exchanger bundles?
faqs.a: Yes. The in-house Level III certification covers UT, RT, MT, PT and VT and does not extend to eddy current, so the proposal names a reviewer whose eddy current certification meets your contract. That reviewer reopens the raw tube files rather than reading only the tube sheet map.

They arrive by secure transfer, are used only for the review you asked for, and are returned or deleted as agreed in the scope. Tell us at the start if your company requires its own transfer platform or a confidentiality agreement.
